title: DNN-Defender: A Victim-Focused In-DRAM Defense Mechanism for Taming Adversarial Weight Attack on DNNs
problem: Attackers exploit RowHammer vulnerability in DRAM to precisely flip bits in DNN model weights, degrading inference accuracy. Existing defenses are either software-based with expensive training overhead or hardware-based with high costs that preserve vulnerable spatial connections.
motivation: As deep learning is deployed in security-sensitive applications, defending against bit-flip attacks on model weights is critical for system security.
method: DNN-Defender is a DRAM-based defense mechanism for quantized DNNs that leverages in-DRAM swapping with a priority protection mechanism. It protects vulnerable weight data by strategically swapping weight locations and prioritizing critical weights to prevent deterministic bit-flips, degrading targeted RowHammer attacks to random attack performance levels.
key_novelty: First DRAM-based victim-focused defense mechanism tailored specifically for quantized DNNs using in-DRAM swapping.
contributions: First DRAM-based victim-focused defense mechanism for quantized DNNs
In-DRAM swapping with priority protection to defend against targeted RowHammer attacks
High protection level with no accuracy drop on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet datasets
No software training overhead or additional hardware overhead

metrics.accuracy: No accuracy drop on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet

limitations: Limitations not discussed in abstract; scalability to larger models and other DNN types not addressed.
